summary:
I reviewed PR #53 head a637c7a357e79614f896ddddf7488e08b5fc9180 (one commit on main 4460ef5) from main's advisor.md, with its risk-tier-2 checklist. The risk tier is 2 because the PR adds files under .claude/. git diff --raw --no-renames shows 4 files, all mode 100644 (no symlink, no submodule), +671 and -0. There are no .checkpoints/ files in it.

1. The head equals what he said yes to. I recomputed both hashes: kept-logs-final-text.md is 97c8165655869d9a... and kl-change-v2.diff is c80dbbb346459d46..., 102 lines. These match history.md:2136 and 2155. I then rebuilt the files with my own node script (.gate/kept-logs-rule/review/compare.mjs), not with kl_build.py. kl_build.py swaps text by search-and-replace; mine inserts each hunk at the line its header names and checks every context line and removed line in place. All four files are byte-equal to git show a637c7a: CHECKPOINTS.md is main's 229 lines, one blank line, then §11 (19 lines); kept-logs.mjs is 313->323 lines; kept-logs.test.mjs is 292->326; REPO_MAP gets its 2 rows. The sha256 values equal compare-head.log's (320c7f25, c9109ab4, 20de2081, d26ef252). §11's two quotes equal history.md:2095-2097 and appear in :2105.

2. The build against its plan (C7-C9, build_plan_changes 1-7). My own runs used the worktree with SHAMBLE_ROLE and KEPT_LOGS_* unset, GNU tar 1.35 and node v22.23.4.
- The suite gives 10 entries: 9 pass and 1 skipped (the dry run alone). "ok 2 - GNU tar unpacks..." has no SKIP, and ok 5 is the second walk.
- The planted copies M4, M11, M12 and M14 differ from the head by exactly their one replacement. Re-runs fail exactly as recorded: M14 only test 5 (actual 0, expected 1), M11 only test 8 (0/2), M9 only test 4 (1/2). The test-engineer re-ran all 14 with the same result.
- The worktree's own full gate (main's node_modules through NODE_PATH; it writes only to the temp folder) gives checks 1-4 and 5b-5d PASS. 5a fails only because Chromium cannot start, the same as gate.log. The PR touches no legacy/, tools/ or .github/ file, so CI's green stands: gate, smoke and toolchain all succeeded on a637c7a (runs 43748934361 and 43748694216).
- The kit tests at the head match main's base runs: checkpoint 27/27, settings 127/127, routine-guard 1107/1107. repo-map-check is OK (122 entries, 109 paths).
- Guard probe: as a day session, main's guard gives no decision on the pack command, as the PR says. The pr-advisor and night-shift roles are both denied.
- Nothing real was packed or deleted. The two real folders' fingerprints today are 3ae12298... and 113c4734..., the same as the dry runs' before and after. .gate/netcode-proof-test/kept-logs/ does not exist. The cache is present and nothing in it is newer than 07:20 UTC. No raw-logs.sha256 is in any commit. The worktree is clean at a637c7a.
- The code matches his words. The second walk sits at kept-logs.mjs:261, after the read-back compare (253-258) and before renameSync (264) and rmSync (273). All three narrowings are there: the .part refusal (225-227), no removal of a .part anywhere, and OLD_BEFORE (44, 299).

3. The review round is in. security-auditor gives APPROVE WITH FINDINGS (SA-KL-1 to SA-KL-4, all Low) and test-engineer gives APPROVE WITH FINDINGS (Lows only), so no push is needed.

4. Two problems are in the PR body, not the head. (a) The logs it links (compare-head.log, evidence-1.log, gate.log, gate-no-smoke.log) are gitignored (.gitignore:7 `*.log`) and are in no commit, so Mustafa and his Advisor cannot open the compare-by-script output or the fingerprints. (b) 13 links have backtick-wrapped targets and do not render as links.

The verdict is for the head as it is. The conditions cover the ready report and the merge.

findings.where: PR #53 body ('The kit files equal...' and 'Evidence' sections); .gitignore:7
findings.what: The body links compare-head.log, evidence-1.log, gate.log and gate-no-smoke.log at e10e1de, but `*.log` is gitignored (.gitignore:7). e10e1de's kl-evidence/ holds only the 17 TAP files, and `git log -- .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/kl-evidence/compare-head.log` is empty. The script's compare output (his ready-report item 3, history.md:2159), the M1-M14 summary, the real folders' fingerprints (they are only in evidence-1.log) and the gate logs exist only on this container's disk. Mustafa and his Advisor cannot open them. The claims are true: I reproduced the compare and the fingerprints. The scripts, the TAP files, the approved texts and history.md:2088-2161 at e10e1de equal the local copies by sha256.
findings.fix: Before the PR is marked ready, commit the five logs on the netcode branch under a name .gitignore does not match (for example .txt), or paste compare-head.log and the two fingerprint lines word for word into the ready report. Then relink. This is a body edit and a notes commit, not a push to PR #53.

findings.where: PR #53 body, 13 links (history.md:2088-2111, :2095-2097, :2105, :2136-2139, :2155-2161, kept-logs-final-text.md, compare-head.log, full.tap, both dry TAPs, evidence-1.log, gate.log, gate-no-smoke.log)
findings.what: Each link target is wrapped in a run of 2 to 14 backticks, for example [history.md:2088-2111](`` https://... ``). Under CommonMark the code span takes priority, so these show as bracketed text plus inline code, not as links. The test-engineer found the same (kl-pr-test.md:39). The line numbers are still in the text, so his words remain cited by line.
findings.fix: In the ready report's body, write plain [text](url) links. The bug looks like it comes from the generator, so check the next body it writes.

findings.what: Four security Lows: (1) a symbolic link swapped into a parent folder between the check and the removal; (2) git() inherits GIT_CONFIG_* from the environment; (3) the cache is recognised by its path and modification times only; (4) the folder is not fsynced after the rename, and renameSync could replace an archive that appeared after the exists check. Each needs a concurrent process run by the same user or deliberate misuse, and the folder or archive stays on every tested path. Fixing any of them would change kit text he said yes to, which needs his yes to the changed lines and falls under KIT-FREEZE-2. A security finding left open keeps the PR needs-mustafa (it already is, as tier 2).
findings.fix: The ready report lists SA-KL-1 to SA-KL-4 as deferred in writing, says where they are tracked (STATUS follow-ups, through docs-keeper), and tells Mustafa they are open. No change to the head.

findings.what: Gaps the test-engineer found: two branches of the second walk are not tested (KLC-F2); several refusal and failure paths are untested but fail safe on reading; the mkfifo case can disappear without a SKIP; the fingerprint pipeline has no pipefail (but the before-values are not the empty hash); the kept-logs tests are not run in CI, like the other kit tests.
findings.fix: Follow-ups, listed in the ready report. A Low never triggers a push.

findings.where: docs/STATUS.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/DECISIONS.md (not in the PR)
findings.what: The PR updates neither STATUS nor ROADMAP, which the every-tier checklist asks for. The approved plan kept the PR to 4 files, matching his 'small and in one place' (history.md:2107), and sent DECISIONS.md to docs-keeper's next pass (KL-5). The body mentions only DECISIONS.md. Until then, STATUS/DECISIONS describe KIT-FREEZE-2 without this rule's exception.
findings.fix: The ready report says STATUS, ROADMAP and DECISIONS.md (his KEPT-LOGS, KL-YES and KL-CHANGE-YES words, and KIT-FREEZE-2 confirmed for this one rule) come in docs-keeper's next pass after the merge.

findings.what: The kept-logs.mjs row says pack removes the folder 'only if all equal the committed list' and does not mention the second walk. It is the approved text: the rows were not part of KL-CHANGE.
findings.fix: No change in this PR. It goes to docs-keeper's next pass as a follow-up.

findings.what: This is a security-auditor note that predates the PR (kl-pr-security.md:44-46), checked by me. In a day session, main allows `node .gate/*.mjs` and `node .gate/*.js` without a prompt, so a script a session writes under .gate/ could remove anything. That is a wider route around '`rm -rf` stays denied' than this PR. It is not a finding on #53.
findings.fix: Record it as a kit follow-up for after the freeze, with its own review and his word. It does not affect this merge.

conditions: C1 (KLH-1): before the PR is marked ready, make the evidence reachable. Commit compare-head.log, evidence-0.log, evidence-1.log, gate.log and gate-no-smoke.log on the netcode branch under a name .gitignore does not match, or paste compare-head.log and the two fingerprint lines word for word into the body. Then relink. Do not push to PR #53's branch for this.
C2 (KLH-2): in the ready report, rewrite all 13 backtick-wrapped links as plain [text](url) links, and keep his words cited by line, not retyped.

C3: turn the body into the ready report. Keep his three items (head a637c7a, the four files, the kit files equal to the approved text with the diff applied, compared by script). Keep the tier-2 table and KIT-FREEZE-2 confirmed for this one rule (history.md:2136). Add both reviewers' verdicts (security-auditor and test-engineer, APPROVE WITH FINDINGS, Lows only) and this advisor verdict for a637c7a. List SA-KL-1 to SA-KL-4 and the test-engineer Lows, each deferred in writing with where it is tracked. Add the settings.json:50-51 note as a separate follow-up. Say that STATUS, ROADMAP and DECISIONS.md come in docs-keeper's next pass after the merge. Fill in 'Decisions needed' and 'For Mustafa' (his go on the merge of #53).

C4: it merges only from a day session, on Mustafa's own go in that session's chat for head a637c7a357e79614f896ddddf7488e08b5fc9180, with gate and smoke green (they are) and a637c7a passed as the expected head. Any new push needs a new advisor review and his go again. Body edits are not pushes.

C5: nothing real is packed or deleted until the PR is on main and the netcode branch has taken main in (history.md:2161). The first real `list` and `pack` follow §11 and C9 (the list commits are data on PR #40's branch, in their own commits, outside the bot fix's line count).
pr_body_check:
I loaded the body with mcp__github__pull_request_read (get; draft, head a637c7a, base 4460ef5, 4 files, +671) and the check runs (6, all success).

What holds, checked against the evidence and my own runs:
- His three ready-report items are there: the head SHA in full, the table of the four files, and the compare-by-script section naming kl_build.py and kl_evidence.py with all four sha256 prefixes. Those prefixes equal compare-head.log and my independent rebuild.
- The (a), (b) and (c) evidence matches full.tap, the dry TAPs and my run: ok 2 with no SKIP, 9 pass and 1 skipped; dry-run files, timings, bytes and read-back counts as stated; ok 5.
- The M1-M14 table matches evidence-1.log and my re-runs of M9, M11 and M14.
- The kit counts (27, 127, 1107), repo-map-check (122/109), the gate statement and the day-session guard claim all hold.
- C8's tier-2 table is there: no existing rule sentence changes; looser than §10's '`rm -rf` stays denied' for exactly his two items, with §11 quoting his words; the three narrowings; the second walk as his requirement; the three limits.
- KIT-FREEZE-2 is recorded as confirmed for this one rule, citing line 2136.
- His words are cited by line at e10e1de and not retyped. history.md:2088-2161 at e10e1de is byte-equal to the local copy, and the approved texts at e10e1de have the right sha256.

What is wrong:
- Four of the linked files are .log files that .gitignore:7 ignores. They are in no commit, so the compare output, the M1-M14 summary, the fingerprints and the gate logs cannot be opened from GitHub (KLH-1).
- 13 links are wrapped in backticks and do not render as links (KLH-2).
- The body is still a progress body ('Results: to come', 'Decisions needed: none yet', 'For Mustafa: nothing yet') and must become the ready report (C3).
to_mustafa:
The pull request for the kept-logs rule (PR #53, version a637c7a) holds exactly what you said yes to: your approved text with the change you approved on top. I rebuilt it with my own script, a different method from the builder's, and all four files match byte for byte. Here is what I re-ran myself:
- the tests: 9 pass, and the GNU tar test ran and was not skipped;
- three of the planted bugs, each caught by its test;
- the gate: everything passes except the browser smoke test, which cannot start in this container; GitHub's own run of it passed;
- the kit's own tests, with the same counts as on main.

Both real log folders are untouched, and their fingerprints still match. Nothing real has been packed or deleted.

Both reviewers approve with minor findings only. The security reviewer's four minor findings all need another process running at the same moment, or deliberate misuse. Fixing them would change lines you approved, so I recommend keeping them as follow-ups.

No code change is needed. Two things in the pull request's description must be fixed before it goes to you for the merge:
- the comparison log and the evidence logs it links were never committed (the repository ignores .log files), so you and your Advisor cannot open them;
- 13 of its links do not work.

The builder fixes both in the final report. Neither changes the code.

Decisions needed:
- KL-MERGE: merge version a637c7a with the security reviewer's four minor findings kept as follow-ups? Why it matters: an open security finding, even a minor one, needs your word. Options: (a) merge as is, findings as follow-ups; (b) fix them first, which means new lines for your yes, a new version and a new review. Recommendation: (a).

For Mustafa:
1. When the final report is posted (working links, the comparison log you can open), say 'merge #53' in a day session's chat. Your go is for version a637c7a. Nothing real is packed or deleted before it is on main and the netcode branch has taken main in.
